messages:
Sofia L: heads up — saw a repeatable p99 tail event during the noon load test. p50 ~ 12ms, p95 ~ 38ms but p99 jumps to ~650ms when concurrency > 220 and KV eviction rate spikes.
Raj P: ugh. is this the same eviction churn we saw last month or a new pattern?
Sofia L: different signal. last month it was steady eviction under sustained QPS. this looks like short-lived "burst+evict" cycles where microbatching amplifies stalls. saw eviction bursts at request spikes, kernel selection falls back to the smaller single-request kernel and that combo kills tail.
Dylan M: can you paste the numbers?
Sofia L: sure — baseline run: QPS=12k, conc=180 -> evict_rate=0.06, p99=220ms. burst run: QPS=16k, conc=240 -> evict_rate=0.23, p99=650ms. microbatch size=4 in both. switching to mb=8 moved p99 to ~420ms but p95 moved up ~10ms.
Mira C: interesting tradeoff. so larger microbatches reduce stalls at the cost of median. do we see kernel fallback logs?
Sofia L: yes. profiling snippet: 
```
evict_rate=0.23 kv_miss=480/s
[profile] hotspot: select_kernel() -> prepare_kv -> copy_kv_pages -> gpu_kernel_choose
stall: 85ms waits in kv_populate + 120ms memcpy on miss path
```
Raj P: that memcpy on miss path is the killer. looks like when the hotset churns we trigger remote copy + synchronous eviction confirmation and that blocks the request thread.
infra-bot: alert: kv-eviction-rate high (1987659999) — affected pods: runtime-xx-7, runtime-xx-9
Dylan M: could we async the eviction confirmation and let the request proceed with a degraded cache hit? maybe fall back to kernel that tolerates missing KV without blocking.
Mira C: idea: change kernel selection heuristic to consider live eviction_rate and kv_miss_ratio before picking small-low-latency kernels; prefer the "batch-tolerant" kernel if eviction_rate > 0.15 for a short window.
Sofia L: +1. also think admission control: if eviction_rate > 0.18, cap concurrency for routes using large-context models to reduce simult. That buys time for rehydration.
Raj P: we should also adjust microbatch logic: dynamic mb sizing (start at 4, scale to 8 if eviction_rate rising). rough rule: if p99 > target*1.8 and evict_rate > 0.12 -> increase mb by factor 2 for next 30s.
Dylan M: there's a perf regression candidate in the kernel selector recent patch — it removed an early-exit that used to skip heavy KV lock when miss_chance low. might be causing extra work during churn. cc @mira to double-check the PR.
Mira C: I'll diff the selector change and instrument a metric: kernel_mismatch_count and selector_latency. also add a fast-path to skip memcpy wait when possible (best-effort progress).
Sofia L: for remediation path — short term: (1) roll config to enable dynamic mb scaling on canary hosts, (2) add selector heuristic gate using eviction_rate, (3) add async eviction ack and fallback kernel.
Raj P: agree. can we get a canary by EOD? roll to 10% traffic and run the same burst trace.
Dylan M: I'll prepare a canary config. command to reproduce load: `loadtest --qps 16000 --concurrency 240 --profile kv-hotset-burst.json` and a profiler command: `runtime-prof --pid $PID --events select_kernel,kv_populate,memcpy --sample 200ms`
Sofia L: thanks. I'll gather traces and post p50/p95/p99 table in this thread after the canary. :thumbsup:
Mira C: logging note — add eviction_rate to per-request trace tags so we can correlate at query-level (helps evals).
Sofia L: noted. going to kick off canary now.
Dylan M: thx — will monitor.
infra-bot: deploy runtime-config/2026-03-17-canary started (10% traffic)
Sofia L: canary running, initial numbers look promising: p99 down from 650ms -> 340ms on canary with selector gate + mb scaling. will run full 30min blast.
